– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testNineEmptyFiles` calls `testCompress252(9, 0)` which attempts to create a 7z archive with 9 empty files. The test fails if the archive is corrupt or incorrectly written when more than 7 empty files are added.

In `testCompress252`, files are added via `addFile`. Each file is named and added to the 7z archive with either empty content (new byte[0]) or some data (byte[]{17}) depending on the parameters.

Looking into `addFile`, we see it creates a `SevenZArchiveEntry`, sets its name, then adds it to the archive and writes data (empty or non-empty). So the issue seems not with file creation or writing empty data.

The next focus is on `SevenZOutputFile` methods on adding entries and closing them. `putArchiveEntry` just adds the entry to an internal list. `closeArchiveEntry` finalizes the current entry, and sets flags like `hasStream` on the entry to indicate if the file has stream data, size, CRCs, etc. For empty files, it sets `hasStream` false and sizes to zero. This part seems correct.

When the archive is closed, `finish` is called. Inside `finish`, it calls `writeHeader` which writes archive metadata. `writeHeader` delegates to `writeFilesInfo`.

In `writeFilesInfo`, several aspects of the files are written to the header, one of which is `writeFileEmptyStreams` that records which files are empty (no streams). `writeFileEmptyStreams` checks if there are any empty streams among files, and writes a bitmask of which files are empty streams.

The bug report says: "If folder contains more than 7 files, incorrect archive is created, often there is a single folder entry with the archive name instead of the files." This implies that the issue might be related to handling of empty files in the header, possibly related to the bitmask for empty streams.

Looking at `writeFileEmptyStreams`, it uses a `BitSet` of size equal to number of files. For every file index, it sets the bit true if the entry has no stream (`!files.get(i).hasStream()`). It then writes this bitset as bits to the header.

The problem likely is that when files exceed 7, `BitSet` bits expand beyond one byte. The encoding of bits may be incorrect or the header size (`writeUint64(header, contents.length)`) or layout may be incorrectly configured, causing the archive reader to interpret this badly. The header writing logic might omit or incorrectly write required markers or lengths, corrupting the archive.

Hence, the root cause is likely in the writing of the empty streams bitmask in `writeFileEmptyStreams`. This bitmask is probably not compliant with the expected 7z specification, causing archives with more than 7 empty files entries to be unreadable or malformed. This fits the observed symptom of only a single folder entry appearing and the inability to properly decode multiple empty entries.

No evidence from recent bug reports is directly relevant here.

Summary:
- The test adds multiple empty files (>7)
- Entries are written with no data streams, and correctly flagged as empty streams
- On finishing archive, empty streams bitset is written in header
- When >7 files, the bitset encoding or header length is incorrect, causing corrupt archive
- Archive readers misinterpret the block, showing wrong archive contents

Therefore, the bug lies in the implementation of `SevenZOutputFile.writeFileEmptyStreams`, specifically in the way the BitSet representing empty streams is serialized in the header.

The solution will be to fix the encoding or header data written in `writeFileEmptyStreams` to handle cases with more than 7 empty files correctly.

---

Next, I will suggest which methods are most relevant to fixing this bug.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
